newsitem.title: USA: Brown & Williamson says claims dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Brown & Williamson says claims dismissed.

text.p: A Maryland judge dismissed nine of 13 counts in an attempt by that state to recover Medicaid expenditures from the tobacco industry, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp said on Wednesday.
However, the court also said that the state was authorized to proceed with its claims that the tobacco companies had violated Maryland's Consumer Protection Act and Antitrust Act.

In today's decision, Maryland circuit court Judge Roger Brown ruled that the state does not have a right to recover Medicaid payments made on behalf of individual smokers, the company said in a prepared statement.
The dismissal applies to a lawsuit known as the State of Maryland v. Philip Morris Inc, et. al., filed on behalf of individuals alleging they were harmed by smoking-related diseases.
"This decision is further proof that Medicaid reimbursement cases are not supported by the law," said Steven McCormick, an attorney for Brown & Williamson.
